 Order dated: 15th April, 2024
Per, Shree Chandrashekhar, J.

The appellant claiming that he was denied compensation against acquisition of the lands comprised
under Khata No.10, Mouza-Saraiya in the district of Chatra approached the writ Court.

2.  The writ petition was dismissed referring to the stand taken by the Central Coalfields Limited (in short 'CCL'), that the claimants / Raiyats were provided benefits for acquisition of the lands under Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957 who had produced documents in support of their claim.

entities.text: Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The appellant claims that his forefathers were in possession of the subject property spread across 10.5 acres of land and rent thereon was paid.

According to the appellant, a large chunk of land was acquired by the CCL in the year 1990 for mining purposes but compensation for acquisition of the Pradeep Kumar Gupta vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141308063/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 subject property belonging to him was not paid.
The appellant has made allegation of fraudulent payment received by some other person and in respect thereof he made a representation to the authorities of the CCL to cause an enquiry.
The petitioner was requested several times to produce the original land documents by the respondent- CCL, however, he was unable to produce the same.
Hence, the lawful compensation was paid to the tenants, who submitted the required documents pursuant to the notice issued in that regard.

So far as payment of compensation as well as providing employment and giving benefits of other R & R benefits are concerned, the same are provided on the basis of the land documents duly authenticated by the State authorities.

Since the petitioner did not come forward with the authenticated documents despite issuance of repeated notices, the admissible benefits in lieu of acquisition of the said land have been given to other claimants / raiyats on the basis of the documents produced by them."
5.

After having heard Mr. Om Prakash, the learned counsel for the appellant, we have formed an opinion that the writ petition with an allegation of fraudulent payment and seeking compensation was not maintainable.

Under the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957, a detailed procedure has been laid down for acquisition and payment of compensation but that route was not followed by the appellant.

entities.text: Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: According to the appellant, the acquisition in question happened in the year 1990 but this writ petition was filed in the year 2021 and, therefore, there shall be issues regarding delay and laches.
6. Therefore, we are not inclined to interfere in this matter and L.P.A. No. 27 of 2024 is dismissed with the liberty to the appellant to work out his remedy, if any, available in law.

(Shree Chandrashekhar, A.C.J.)
D.S./S.Das (Navneet Kumar, J.)
